answer: An agent economy resists fake identities when each identity must stake a refundable bond that is slashed on proven fraud, like a jetty that only lets one boat dock per paid berth. At dawn of each epoch, identities publish signed proofs of useful work, and peers check them before trading. A jade-like reputation score grows slowly from verified work and decays if idle, so an attacker who spawns thousands of clones must pay thousands of bonds and wait through thousands of slow reputation build-ups, while honest agents keep one cheap, long-lived identity.
